title: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 32](/bible/deuteronomy/32)

**[Deuteronomy 32:1-3](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v1)</sup> Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v2)</sup> My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v3)</sup> Because I will publish the name of the Lord: ascribe ye greatness unto our God.

- Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. The song opens by calling heaven and earth to witness, just as Moses said in chapter 31.
- Notice how the verses run together: my doctrine shall drop as the rain, and then, because I will publish the name of the Lord. Doctrine and the name go together, and greatness is ascribed unto our God.

**[Deuteronomy 32:4-5](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v4)</sup> He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v5)</sup> They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation.

- He is the Rock, his work is perfect, all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. The song gives the Most High his praise first, then turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves.
- They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 2:21](/bible/jeremiah/2#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/2#v21)</sup> Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?

    The Most High planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and thou art turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine.

**[Deuteronomy 32:6](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v6)</sup> Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?

- Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land. Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? Hath he not made thee, and established thee?
- Isaiah recounts the lovingkindness of the Most High toward the house of Israel: he said, surely they are my people, children that will not lie, so he was their Savior. In all our affliction he was afflicted; whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us, and in his love and in his pity he redeemed us and carried us all the days of old.
- How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 63:7-10](/bible/isaiah/63#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/isaiah/63#v7)</sup> I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/isaiah/63#v8)</sup> For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/63#v9)</sup> In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/isaiah/63#v10)</sup> But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.

    He was Israel's Savior and carried them all the days of old, but they rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, therefore he was turned to be their enemy.
  - **[Acts 7:51](/bible/acts/7#v51)**
    > <sup>[51](/bible/acts/7#v51)</sup> Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.

    Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.

**[Deuteronomy 32:7](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v7)</sup> Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.

- Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you.
- The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee.
- Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers: study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers; that is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves.
- Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

  Precepts:
  - **[Job 8:8](/bible/job/8#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/job/8#v8)</sup> For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

    Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers.
  - **[Psalms 44:1](/bible/psalms/44#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/44#v1)</sup> We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

    We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
  - **[Romans 15:4](/bible/romans/15#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/romans/15#v4)</sup> For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

    Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

**[Deuteronomy 32:8-9](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v8)</sup> When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v9)</sup> For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.

- When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. You thought God wants everybody to just come together and hold hands? The God of this Bible has been a God of division from day one; he separated the sons of Adam according to where he had to place the children of Israel, meaning this world revolves around Israel.
- For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel he kept for himself: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 17:17](/bible/sirach/17#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/sirach/17#v17)</sup> For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion:

    In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel is the Lord's portion.

**[Deuteronomy 32:10](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v10)</sup> He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.

- He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye. The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye.
- Zechariah shows who that people is: deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans? We are Zion, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there.
- He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

  Precepts:
  - **[Zechariah 2:6-8](/bible/zechariah/2#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/zechariah/2#v6)</sup> Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/zechariah/2#v7)</sup> Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/zechariah/2#v8)</sup> For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.

    Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon, for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
  - **[Psalms 137:7-8](/bible/psalms/137#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/137#v7)</sup> Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/137#v8)</sup> O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.

    Edom is remembered against the day of Jerusalem, and the daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed; this shows who Zion dwells with.

**[Deuteronomy 32:11-14](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v11)</sup> As an eagle stirreth up her nest, fluttereth over her young, spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings:
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v12)</sup> So the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v13)</sup> He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the increase of the fields; and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock;
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v14)</sup> Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the fat of kidneys of wheat; and thou didst drink the pure blood of the grape.

- As an eagle stirreth up her nest and beareth her young on her wings, so the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him. The Most High used no idol of wood or stone to lead us through the wilderness and protect us from the nations; he did that alone.
- He made him ride on the high places of the earth, to eat the increase of the fields, honey out of the rock, butter of kine and milk of sheep, the fat of lambs and rams, and the pure blood of the grape. This is the journey through the wilderness, how Israel came through all those nations and acquired wealth and provision from the Most High's own hand.

**[Deuteronomy 32:15](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v15)</sup> But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.

- But Jeshurun, meaning Israel, waxed fat, and kicked; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.
- Waxing fat is not about being overweight; [Deuteronomy 8](/bible/deuteronomy/8) explains it. When thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and thy herds and thy silver and thy gold are multiplied, then thine heart is lifted up and thou forgettest the Lord thy God which brought thee out of the house of bondage.
- With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 8:12-14](/bible/deuteronomy/8#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/8#v12)</sup> Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein;
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/8#v13)</sup> And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied;
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/8#v14)</sup> Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;

    Lest when thou hast eaten and art full and all thou hast is multiplied, thine heart be lifted up and thou forget the Lord thy God.

**[Deuteronomy 32:16-17](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v16)</sup> They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v17)</sup> They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.

- They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods; they sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.
- What are examples of new gods? Islam came about in 622 AD, some six hundred years after Christ. The familiar image of Christ painted in the Renaissance era is a new thing under the sun. Even Buddha, whom people think is ancient, came on the scene between the sixth and fourth centuries BC; our kingdom had already been split and carried captive into Babylon before anybody heard of a Buddha.
- These are new gods that our people go crazy over today, and the Most High said we would come to that estate.

**[Deuteronomy 32:18](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v18)</sup> Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.

- Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee. When it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful.
- Who is that Rock? Paul says our fathers drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses; he was with Israel in the wilderness.
- David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Corinthians 10:4](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v4)</sup> And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.

    They all drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
  - **[2 Samuel 22:2-3](/bible/2-samuel/22#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/22#v2)</sup> And he said, The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/22#v3)</sup> The God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.

    David says the Lord is my rock, and then the God of my rock; in him will I trust.
  - **[Psalms 110:1](/bible/psalms/110#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/110#v1)</sup> The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

    The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand.
  - **[1 Corinthians 11:3](/bible/1-corinthians/11#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-corinthians/11#v3)</sup> But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.

    The head of every man is Christ, and the head of Christ is God.

**[Deuteronomy 32:19-21](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v19)</sup> And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v20)</sup> And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v21)</sup> They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.

- When the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons and of his daughters; he said, I will hide my face from them, for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.
- This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom: when Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God, and Christ called them a generation of vipers.
- They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God, and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel; no, the ones which are not a people are also Israel.
- Isaiah says within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and Hosea says of the northern kingdom, ye are not my people, yet in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
- The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

  Precepts:
  - **[Matthew 23:33](/bible/matthew/23#v33)**
    > <sup>[33](/bible/matthew/23#v33)</sup> Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

    Christ called the froward, faithless generation of his day serpents and a generation of vipers.
  - **[Isaiah 7:8](/bible/isaiah/7#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/isaiah/7#v8)</sup> For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.

    Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim, head of the northern kingdom, be broken, that it be not a people.
  - **[Hosea 1:9-10](/bible/hosea/1#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/hosea/1#v9)</sup> Then said God, Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hosea/1#v10)</sup> Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.

    Ye are not my people; yet in the place where that was said, it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.

**[Deuteronomy 32:22-25](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v22)</sup> For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell, and shall consume the earth with her increase, and set on fire the foundations of the mountains.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v23)</sup> I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v24)</sup> They shall be burnt with hunger, and devoured with burning heat, and with bitter destruction: I will also send the teeth of beasts upon them, with the poison of serpents of the dust.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v25)</sup> The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the suckling also with the man of gray hairs.

- For a fire is kindled in mine anger; I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them: burning hunger, bitter destruction, and the teeth of beasts sent upon them.
- You have seen the clips from the civil rights movement, the canines sent at our people to rip at them with their teeth. That was a fulfillment of prophecy: the Most High said he would send the teeth of beasts against us.
- The sword without, and terror within, destroying young man and virgin, the suckling with the man of gray hairs: the sword of the other nations, and famine and drought as well. This prophecy had to happen against us because we served other gods.

**[Deuteronomy 32:26](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v26)</sup> I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men:

- I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. What corners? Isaiah shows the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth: the scattering was worldwide.
- What nation of people has been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth by slave trades, the transatlantic, the sub-Saharan, the silk road? The so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. This never happened to the people claiming our heritage; it is further proof of who the children of Israel are.
- The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 11:12](/bible/isaiah/11#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/isaiah/11#v12)</sup> And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

    He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
  - **[Psalms 83:4](/bible/psalms/83#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/83#v4)</sup> They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

    They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

**[Deuteronomy 32:27-30](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v27)</sup> Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v28)</sup> For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v29)</sup> O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v30)</sup> How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up?

- Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this. The Most High would not let the enemy think they accomplished the complete destruction of the Israelites by their own hand; that is why, after a certain amount of time, he begins waking us up, and why we are starting to remember who we are this day.
- For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them. O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end. If you knew exactly what disaster was coming and when, you would set every alarm; our forefathers were told all these atrocities ahead of time and still did not consider it.
- How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up? How could we be conquered the way we were, thousands rounded up by a few, unless the Most High allowed it? It had to be the Lord.

**[Deuteronomy 32:31-33](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v31)</sup> For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v32)</sup> For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter:
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v33)</sup> Their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel venom of asps.

- For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges.
- For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: that is why the sins of Sodom show up among our people today, even paraded as pride. The Most High said our vine became the vine of Sodom; their grapes are grapes of gall, their wine is the poison of dragons.
- Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures? These prophecies were sealed up with the Most High until their time.

**[Deuteronomy 32:34-36](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v34)**

> <sup>[34](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v34)</sup> Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v35)</sup> To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v36)</sup> For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants, when he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left.

- To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand. After he let these nations deceive and oppress us for so long, the Most High will show who God really is; but he had to let us humble ourselves first for serving all those false gods.
- For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants: he will change his mind, and instead of inflicting wrath upon us he will save us.
- When he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left: when he sees that we have fallen to our lowest estate possible, then he moves.

**[Deuteronomy 32:37-38](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v37)**

> <sup>[37](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v37)</sup> And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted,
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v38)</sup> Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.

- And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted? Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you.
- The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us.
- Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

  Precepts:

    > <sup>[27](/bible/jeremiah/2#v27)</sup> Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/jeremiah/2#v28)</sup> But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.

    They turned their back unto the Most High, but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us; let the gods they made save them, for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods.

**[Deuteronomy 32:39](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v39)**

> <sup>[39](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v39)</sup> See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.

- See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.
- A statue you made with your hands cannot kill a thing and cannot make alive; the true God does both. That is the terrible God we serve, the God of our people, and once his people get back on his good side, the nations that touched the apple of his eye have judgment coming.

**[Deuteronomy 32:40-42](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v40)**

> <sup>[40](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v40)</sup> For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v41)</sup> If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v42)</sup> I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy.

- For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever. The Most High will eventually turn back to save us; he will stop hiding his face and come to our defense.
- If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me. I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy.
- The Most High takes revenge for the captives, because he is the God of the people that have been in captivity over and over again. In the churches they never read this; they never knew that God is this way, and it shows what they really think about him.

**[Deuteronomy 32:43](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v43)**

> <sup>[43](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v43)</sup> Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.

- Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.
- Read through the Bible: Christ put to death, James put to death, Peter put to death, and since the Bible was written more prophets have lost their lives for the truth, and it will continue. The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto the Most High, and the souls of the just complain continually, asking when he will act; and he answers, I will surely avenge them.
- This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

> <sup>[48](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v48)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses that selfsame day, saying,
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v49)</sup> Get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is over against Jericho; and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel for a possession:
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v50)</sup> And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people; as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people:
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v51)</sup> Because ye trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah–Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[52](/bible/deuteronomy/32#v52)</sup> Yet thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither unto the land which I give the children of Israel.

- That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses: get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan; and die in the mount, as Aaron died in mount Hor, because ye trespassed against me at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.
- The account is in Numbers 20: the people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter.
- Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.
